sections.h2: Who bills and assesses property tax in Craven County, NC?
sections.html:
The Craven County Tax Administration at 226 Pollock Street in New Bern handles both jobs: it appraises real estate and it collects the bills. The counter is staffed from eight in the morning until five on weekdays. Appraisal questions go to the real estate appraisal division at 252-636-6640.

The department also runs separate divisions for tax collection (252-636-6605), business personal property and non-business personal property. Motor vehicle tax follows its own tag-and-tax system through the state, and the department's menu covers gap bills for vehicles, so a house seller can ignore those unless a closing statement mentions one.

The county site names eight municipalities: Bridgeton, Cove City, Dover, Havelock, New Bern, River Bend, Trent Woods and Vanceboro. Land area totals 706.57 square miles, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate shows 105,025 residents.

sections.h2: What is the Craven County property tax rate?
sections.html:
With its 2026-2027 budget, the board of commissioners held the rate at 44.48 cents per $100 of assessed value. That figure is the county's own levy. Confirm any town or district charge stacked on it using the 2026 tax rates document on the county site.

Rates apply to assessed value after any exclusion you have been granted. The state exclusions come in three kinds. Under the elderly or disabled exclusion, the larger of $25,000 or 50% of a permanent residence's appraised value is set aside, and the 2026 income limit is $38,800. A disabled veteran has the first $45,000 of appraised value excluded, with no age or income test. The circuit breaker limits the bill to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% for income above that limit but within 150% of it; NCDOR prints that upper figure as $58,200 for 2026.

Value and rate come from different decisions. The county's revaluation FAQ explains that a revaluation sets market value, while the commissioners set the rate for budget needs. A higher assessment therefore does not by itself mean a higher rate, and a held rate can still produce a larger bill when the value goes up.

The county's tax menu has a page for each program. Owners apply on Form AV-9 at the assessor's office, and the county must take one up to June 1 of the preceding year.

sections.h2: What dates matter on a Craven County tax bill?
sections.html:
Billing opens September 1 and interest-free payment ends January 5. The collection division's list of dates is condensed below.

Craven County tax collection calendar as printed by the Tax Collection Division
DateWhat happens
September 1Bills are due (state law)
January 5Final interest-free day
January 6Taxes are delinquent
Mid-JanuaryDelinquent tax notices mailed
Mid-FebruaryDebt setoff notices mailed, and attachment and garnishment proceed
March 31Final day to pay and stay off the published delinquent list

Under G.S. 105-360, interest opens at 2% on January 6 and climbs three-fourths of one percent for every month or fraction beginning February 1.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Craven County property tax bill?
sections.html:
• Online at my.cravencountync.gov. A lookup by name, address or parcel number leads to the bill, and the platform allows scheduled and partial payments.
  • By mail to Craven County Tax Collector, PO Box 1128, New Bern, NC 28563-1128.
  • At the counter, 226 Pollock Street, with check, cash, money order or card, or in the drop box at the front right of the building. Cash does not belong in the drop box.

The county page for online payments points to a payment vendor for help, and the tax menu lists pre-payments and a delinquent payment assistance page. For delinquent bills, the county refers owners to NCHomeownerAssistance.gov and the state hotline 1-855-696-2423.

Before a sale, request a payoff amount covering this year and any unpaid earlier years. A lien for real property tax attaches to the parcel as of its listing date (G.S. 105-355), which is why a payoff letter protects both sides.

sections.h2: When did Craven County last revalue property, and when is the next time?
sections.html:
Tax year 2023 carried the most recent revaluation, and tax year 2028 is next. Notices of new value went out the week of February 27, 2023, and appeals were due by 5:00 p.m. on May 22, 2023.

Before that, Craven County's last revaluation was 2016. The commissioners had shortened the cycle to six years in 2011 and to four years after 2016, but Hurricane Florence in 2018 caused the planned 2020 revaluation to slip to 2023. G.S. 105-286 sets eight years as the longest gap. Counties of 75,000 or more can be pushed into an earlier cycle when sales assessment ratios drift under .85 or over 1.15, and Craven says its population falls in that group.

A Revaluation 2028 page already exists, and its comparable-sales search tool is marked "coming February 2028." Values are set as market value on January 1 of the revaluation year.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Craven County property value?
sections.html:
File a signed appeal form with the county assessor ahead of the date printed on your notice. For the 2023 revaluation the county set that deadline at the board's adjournment date, May 22, 2023.

  • Attach comparable sales dated on or before January 1 of the revaluation year, photos of the property's condition, and a recent appraisal or market analysis if you have one.
  • The owner, an attorney or an agent under power of attorney can sign. A close family member may also appear when the owner cannot, such as during unexpected military duty or a hospital stay.
  • An appraiser reviews your file and mails a result that may raise the value, cut it or leave it alone.
  • If you still disagree, the Board of Equalization and Review takes the case, with a hearing letter sent at least 15 days ahead.
  • Bring copies of your evidence for the seven board members.

The Property Tax Commission is the next stop after the board. Written notice must be filed within 30 days of the board's mailing date, and the assessor gets a copy (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Craven County homes?
sections.html:
Census estimates for 2020-2024 put the middle owner-occupied home at $231,600, and owners live in 68.4% of homes. Household income has a median of $65,873, and gross rent a median of $1,110 monthly.

Residents 65 or older make up 24.2% of the population, so the elderly exclusion and circuit breaker matter to many owners. The county counts 50,334 housing units, issued 553 building permits in 2025, and has 10,968 veterans, so the disabled veteran exclusion also reaches a meaningful number of owners.

Other items on the county's tax menu that can change a bill or a listing:

  • A Present Use Value Exclusion page.
  • Historic Properties, Builders Exclusion, Religious Uses Exemption and Antique Airplane and Automobile Exclusion pages.
  • A gross receipts rental tax report and an occupancy and tourism development tax form, which matter to anyone selling a rental.
  • Change of mailing address forms, so a seller's final bill reaches the right place after closing.

faqs.q: When are Craven County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are due September 1, and January 5 is the last interest-free day. Delinquency starts January 6, when 2% interest begins.

faqs.q: What is the Craven County property tax rate?
faqs.a: For fiscal year 2026-2027 the county rate stayed at 44.48 cents per $100. The 2026 tax rates document shows any town or district charge.

faqs.q: When is the next Craven County revaluation?
faqs.a: The county's Revaluation 2028 page says the next countywide revaluation applies to tax year 2028. The last one took effect in 2023.

faqs.q: Who can appeal a Craven County valuation?
faqs.a: Owners, attorneys and agents holding power of attorney may sign. File comparable sales, photos or an appraisal with the county assessor by the date on your notice.

faqs.q: What follows if a Craven County bill is unpaid after January 5?
faqs.a: Delinquency begins January 6. Notices follow in mid-January, setoff notices and garnishment steps in mid-February, and a newspaper list appears after March 31.
